input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only us and fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-sided rather than mutual, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term (not just personnel involved in the Services), bars "engage" as well as solicit (an effective no-hire, which is walk-away territory), runs eighteen months from termination rather than twelve months from the end of the person's involvement, and contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no no-hire commitment. We propose the fallback formulation (mutual, involved personnel only, twelve months, customary carve-outs, no no-hire) as the smallest workable edit given the bargain already reflected in § 12.3.

proposal.summary: Make § 12.4 mutual, limit to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of their involvement, delete the no-hire ("engage"), and add general-advertising/unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We narrowed this to a mutual, twelve-month non-solicit covering only personnel directly involved in the Services, removed the "engage" no-hire element, and added the customary general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. Our playbook does not accept a one-sided no-hire over all Vendor personnel, and the current wording also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: For twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither party will directly solicit for employment any personnel of the other party who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict either party from hiring any person who responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment activity not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or who approaches that party on an unsolicited basis, and neither party is subject to any no-hire obligation.
